Subject: Inference model shortlist, quick tradeoffs, and next steps

Hi Sophie / Daniel —

Thanks for taking the demo yesterday. Quick recap and the model shortlist we discussed, plus concrete next steps so we stay moving this week. I attached the shortlist spreadsheet and the benchmark PDF; prompt set is attached as a JSONL stub for your eval team.

High-level recommendation (short):
- Pilot with rw-3b-instruct-quant (balanced): best mix of latency and token cost for interactive support flows.
- Tiered fallback: rw-70b-sft (hosted optimized) for high-quality summarization tasks where latency can tolerate ~200–300ms extra cost.
- Cost-saver path for bulk generation: rw-1.3b-quant-bf (batch-optimized) for nightly background generation and reranking.

Why these: brief tradeoffs
- rw-3b-instruct-quant: p95 latency for 512-token context ~140ms (single-request, no batching), estimated hosted cost ~$45 / 1M prompt+gen tokens. Quality is solid on our instruction suite (F1 ~0.78 on Acme-sim tests) and low regression risk during quantized runs.
- rw-70b-sft: best in-class quality on summarization and legal-extract prompts (ROUGE/QA lift ~+8–12% vs 3B). P95 latency ~320ms; cost ~ $420 / 1M tokens in hosted mode. Use as a canary for sensitive outputs.
- rw-1.3b-quant-bf: throughput-first; when batched at night we hit 10–15x throughput with p95 per-token latency ~60ms but not suitable for chat. Cost ~ $12 / 1M tokens.

Benchmarks & artifacts (attached / linked):
- benchmarks-20261129.pdf (incl. p50/p95/p99 latency traces, token-cost calc, eval prompts)
- acme-shortlist-20261130.xlsx (model matrix + suggested rollout plan and gating prompts)
- prompt-set-acme-v1.jsonl (100 curated prompts: 35 summarization, 40 chat/support, 25 rerank/test cases)

Open risks and asks we want to confirm:
1) Latency SLO: you mentioned 250ms p95 for UI flows; confirm whether that applies to all chat types or just short-support replies. If 250ms is firm, we should prioritize 3B and fallback to 70B only for async jobs.
2) Data residency: any PII/sensitive data that must stay in a VPC? Marissa—please confirm the compliance checklist I attached to the Drive link.
3) Volume estimate: Sophie, please send top-line monthly token estimate for both real-time chat and nightly batch within EOD Thursday so we can firm up cost projection.

Next steps (proposed):
- Today: I’ll share benchmark links and the prompt pack (done, attached).
- Tue: Technical deep-dive with Karthik and your infra team (30–45m).
- Thu: Pricing & pilot contract draft from Ben & Marissa once we have rough monthly usage.

If that schedule works, I’ll book the TD session — propose Tue 11/3 11:00 PT (open to alternatives).

Thanks,

— Hannah Schmitt
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0123

We’ll try to pull together a ballpark volume estimate by Thursday.

Subject: Re: Inference model shortlist, quick tradeoffs, and next steps

Sophie — great questions, thanks. Answers inline and a few attachments/links for the team.

1) rw-3b-instruct-quant latency context: the p95s in the PDF are measured on a mixed traffic trace; for your stated mix (120 token context + 80 token generation) we see ~155ms p95 without batching, ~95–110ms p95 when using continuous batching (recommended for chat with 20–30ms batching overhead). I added a small table in the PDF page 6 with the per-context breakdown.

2) rw-70b-sft reduced-width: yes — we can run the 70B with a low-precision matrix path (4-bit) which reduces cost ~28% and latency ~15% in our hosted environment; quality drop is small for extractive summarization but noticeable on creative rewriting. Recommendation: enable reduced-width for non-creative summarization jobs; keep full precision for critical outputs.

3) Nightly batch integration: Redwood exposes a batch endpoint that accepts NDJSON bundles and a job callback. For simple nightly jobs you can post the file to S3 and we’ll pull or you can push via the endpoint. We recommend S3 + job callback for large nightly runs (less egress and more resumability). Integration effort: ~2–3 dev days to add the push + post-processing handlers on your side depending on your infra.

Pilot proposal (concrete):
- Week 1–2: sandbox pilot with rw-3b-instruct-quant (10k daily messages) to validate latency & quality on your real prompts.
- Week 3–4: run A/B vs rw-70b-sft on a 5% traffic slice for summarization screens.
- Ongoing: nightly batch on rw-1.3b-quant-bf for bulk reranks.

I’ve added suggested gating checks in the spreadsheet (accuracy thresholds, p95 latency, cost thresholds). If you confirm 250ms for the support widget as the firm SLO, we’ll lock the pilot to rw-3b and only route to 70B for post-hoc offline summaries.

Drive links: https://drive.redwood/reports/acme/benchmarks-20261129 (benchmark folder)

Ben / Marissa / Karthik — can we:
- Ben: prepare ballpark pilot pricing (monthly run-rate) assuming 100k chat messages / month and the tiered fallback usage (estimate in the spreadsheet).
- Marissa: add compliance/VPC checklist follow-up item and confirm any additional artifacts Acme requires for SOC2 evidence.
- Karthik: run an infra checklist (S3 path, callback URL, network egress) and propose a 30–45m TD time slots.

If all good, I’ll schedule the TD for Tue 12/1 11:00 PT.

— Hannah
